organizations_boardelections.any_composi: Any composition change — a seat added by the scale, a vacancy, a transfer — clears the chair and re-triggers the joint election by the full board · Art. III §6 · WF-ORG-05.
Any composition change — a seat added by the scale, a vacancy, a transfer — re-triggers the joint chair election · Art. III §6 · WF-ORG-04 → WF-ORG-05.
organizations_boardelections.board_elect: Board elections reuse the public-election engine end to end — owner and worker races carry an electorate_type (owners / workers) and run the same protected STV count. The chair is the one board-internal vote: a ranked-choice ballot of the entire seated board, won at a majority of all seated seats.
organizations_boardelections.chair_elect: Chair elected jointly by the entire Board · Art. III §6
organizations_boardelections.chair_seate: chair: {winner} — seated as joint chair · public record kind certification
organizations_boardelections.co_determin: Co-determination provisions a board on the owner track first (F-ORG-003); the worker track and its seats appear once the organization crosses the first-seat threshold (CLK-13). The owner-track administration form below provisions it.
organizations_boardelections.composition: Composition changed — a fresh joint chair election is required before the board acts.
Composition invalid — a worker-track election is required before the board acts
organizations_boardelections.eligible_ow: eligible owners see the race on their ballot surface
organizations_boardelections.eligible_wo: eligible workers see the race on their ballot surface
organizations_boardelections.final_round: Final round of the certified worker-track count.
organizations_boardelections.gold_tick_t: Gold tick = the Droop quota; reaching it elects a candidate. Final round of the certified count.
organizations_boardelections.joint_chair: Joint chair — elected by the entire board (RCV)
organizations_boardelections.no_chair_el: No chair election on record yet.
organizations_boardelections.no_owner_tr: No owner-track election has run — schedule one to fill the vacant owner seats.
organizations_boardelections.no_seats_fi: No seats filled yet — winners of the owner and worker tracks seat here, then the board elects its chair.
organizations_boardelections.no_worker_t: No worker-track election has run yet — the vacant worker seats await the count. The system opens this election automatically when the scale adds a seat (CLK-13).

No worker track — the first worker seat appears at the CLK-13 minimum headcount. Below that threshold the owner side governs per the organization's structure rules (the live value and the scale are on the co-determination page).
organizations_boardelections.opens_the_s: opens the same two-phase open ballot as a public election
organizations_boardelections.shareholder: shareholders elect the owner side · the same Droop-quota STV as a public election · Art. III §4, §6
organizations_boardelections.the_joint_c: The joint chair election opens once the board has at least two seated members (Art. III §6). It re-triggers on any composition change.
organizations_boardelections.the_winner_: the winner must reach a majority of all seated board seats
organizations_boardelections.this_organi: This organization has no board yet.
organizations_boardelections.this_track_: this track exists because the organization crossed the first-seat threshold · CLK-13; its {workerSeats} seat(s) come from the uniform co-determination scale · CLK-14 · co-determination scaling →
organizations_boardelections.three_count: Three counts seat one board: shareholders elect the owner track by STV, workers elect the worker track by STV, and then the entire board jointly elects its chair by ranked choice. Voting itself happens on the public ballot surfaces — the counts published here are the record.
organizations_cgcdetail.a_cgc_is_subject: A CGC is subject to the same regulation as any private peer; its public ownership confers no regulatory privilege · Art. III §5.
organizations_cgcdetail.a_common_good_co: A Common Good Corporation is a public enterprise chartered by a legislature to provide goods or services to its jurisdiction. It competes and is regulated exactly like its private peers — with one permanent difference: everything it creates belongs to everyone.

A Common Good Corporation is public property held for the common good. The legislature charters it (F-LEG-019), an executive department oversees it, and its intellectual property is perpetually public domain (Art. III §5). It is otherwise regulated exactly like a private enterprise — and runs the same co-determination scale as every other board (Art. III §6).
organizations_cgcdetail.co_determination: Co-determination — the Board of Governors stands where shareholders would
organizations_cgcdetail.every_work_is_pu: Every work is public domain from the moment of creation
organizations_cgcdetail.every_work_this_: Every work this corporation produces is public domain from the moment of creation — universally, eternally, irreversibly · Art. III §5.
organizations_cgcdetail.in_a_common_good: In a Common Good Corporation the Board of Governors stands where shareholders would — the owner side runs on the share system everywhere else.
organizations_cgcdetail.no_works_registe: No works registered yet — the public-domain rule attaches at creation, not at registration.
organizations_cgcdetail.only_the_legisla: Only the legislature may reorganize, sell, or dissolve a CGC ( · WF-ORG-09); existing public-domain IP status survives any sale.
organizations_cgcdetail.public_domain_de: Public-domain dedications — status is always public domain (append-only, irreversible)
organizations_cgcdetail.regulated_identi: Regulated identically to private peers — hardened
organizations_cgcdetail.the_legislature_: The legislature creates; the executive oversees · Art. III §5.
organizations_cgcdetail.there_is_no_stat: There is no status field — public domain is the only value. Dedication is irreversible.
organizations_codetermination.any_compos: Any composition change — a seat added by the scale, a vacancy, a transfer — triggers a fresh joint chair election by the entire board. The board is valid only while its composition matches the scale; until the worker-track election and the joint chair election complete, the board cannot act.
organizations_codetermination.chair_elec: chair elected jointly by the entire board · Art. III §6
organizations_codetermination.co_determi: Co-determination state of every live board
organizations_codetermination.compositio: Composition change re-triggers the joint chair election
organizations_codetermination.no_board_h: No board has reached the first-seat threshold yet.
organizations_codetermination.no_entity_: No entity bound — drag the slider to explore the published formula at this instance's resolved thresholds. Append ?org=<id> (or follow a row below) to bind the meter to a live organization's own numbers.
organizations_codetermination.one_boards: One boards table, one co-determination engine. The worker-side seat count is a stored snapshot written only by the protected co-determination service — this surface renders it, never recomputes it. The owner side differs by entity (a stock company's shareholders elect their seats; a Common Good Corporation's and a department's governors are appointed), but the worker-side scale is byte-for-byte identical, which is exactly what the applies-equally table proves.
organizations_codetermination.one_row_pe: one row per live board across private enterprises, Common Good Corporations, and executive departments · the owner side runs shareholder-elected or appointed governors, but the worker-side scale is identical · Art. III §6
organizations_codetermination.the_active: The active worker headcount at which the first worker-elected seat is required. Amendable within bounds — it {bounds_gloss}.
organizations_codetermination.the_headco: The headcount at which worker seats reach parity with the owner side — the ceiling. Amendable within bounds — it {bounds_gloss}.
organizations_codetermination.the_scale_: The scale applies equally — every board, one engine

The scale binds from the first qualifying organization — the first time an employer's active worker headcount crosses the CLK-13 minimum ({clk13}), its row appears here flipping below → scaling · 1 seat with composition_valid=false and a worker-track election. The explorer above is fully functional in the meantime.
organizations_codetermination.the_worker: The worker track and the joint chair election run on the elections machinery — administered from a board's board-elections page.
organizations_codetermination.when_a_com: When a company employs {clk13} or more people, its workers start electing seats on its board. The first worker seat arrives at that threshold, and worker seats grow evenly until they match the owners' seats at {clk14} workers. The formal name for this is co-determination. The same scale applies to private companies, Common Good Corporations, and government departments.
organizations_orgdetail.a_candidate_requ: A candidate requests (F-CAN-002); the agent grants (F-ORG-002), which is forced public and confers R-07 on the candidate. There is no faction registration — endorsements are polymorphic rows · ledger #q1.
organizations_orgdetail.a_contract_takes: A contract takes effect only with both signatures — the engine rejects effect before both.
organizations_orgdetail.a_recurring_labo: A recurring labor contract backs the registration; it counts toward headcount once the organization countersigns.
organizations_orgdetail.a_stable_identif: A stable identifier for the package (e.g. bylaws-2031).
organizations_orgdetail.an_organization_: An organization's public profile — ownership, board, endorsements, and the join paths. Endorsement linkage feeds proportionality, never a faction layer; the worker headcount feeds the co-determination scale. Everything here is a public record (Art. II §2 · Art. III).
organizations_orgdetail.apply_for_this_o: Apply for this organization's ownership class — the organization accepts per its bylaws; R-24 derives on acceptance.
organizations_orgdetail.co_determination: Co-determination begins at {min} workers (CLK-13); until then ownership governs per its structure rules.
organizations_orgdetail.confirm_your_res: Confirm your residency to join (Art. I).
Confirm your residency to register as a worker (Art. I).
organizations_orgdetail.endorsement_link: Endorsement linkage feeds proportionality — not a faction layer.
organizations_orgdetail.internal_package: Internal packages never override the constitutional forms — a package key may not collide with a form ID.
organizations_orgdetail.this_profile_is_: This profile is a public record. The endorsement handshake, the membership and worker join paths, and the co-determination scale all run on one organization model — there is no faction layer.
organizations_orgdetail.worker_headcount: Worker headcount feeds the co-determination scale · CLK-13 / CLK-14.
organizations_orgdetail.you_are_register: You are registered as a worker.
organizations_registry.any_associated_re: Any associated resident may register one — association is the only requirement (Art. I).
organizations_registry.common_good_corpo: Common Good Corporations are not self-registered — the legislature creates them by act (F-LEG-019 · WF-ORG-08).
organizations_registry.endorsing_and_the: "Endorsing" and the co-determination tiers are derived display states — read from live endorsement rows and the worker headcount against the CLK-13 / CLK-14 thresholds — never stored statuses. The stored machine is registration → active, with the transfer, conversion, and dissolution branches.
organizations_registry.every_registered_: Every registered organization where you live — parties, businesses, nonprofits, and public companies share one open list. Anyone who lives here can start one.
organizations_registry.no_organizations_: No organizations match the current filters.
No organizations registered in your association chain.
organizations_registry.registration_is_a: Registration is an absolute right of any associated resident (Art. I, Economic Freedom) — you just need an active residency association first.
organizations_transfersconversions.a_con: A conversion request () routes to the legislature — a request, not an act. Both directions are legislature-only; the legislature authorizes the conversion by act (). Public-domain IP irreversibly stays public — new works after privatization follow private rules.
organizations_transfersconversions.acqui: Acquisition vote — ordinary majority of all serving; the only path overriding owner consent · owner ruling #13.
organizations_transfersconversions.an_or: An organization's ownership can change five ways, and this page shows all five: sold by mutual agreement, acquired by the legislature when a monopoly is found, converted between public and private, restructured within private hands, or wound down. Only the monopoly path ever overrides the owners' consent — and it carries a protected compensation floor.
organizations_transfersconversions.found: Founding governor seats offered to the prior board
organizations_transfersconversions.four_: Four paths, one principle: ownership never moves against its owner's will except where the constitution names a public interest (monopoly), and even then at fair-market compensation. Public↔private conversion runs through the legislature; public-domain IP stays public irreversibly (Art. III §5).
organizations_transfersconversions.inter: Internal restructuring needs no legislature — owner consent per the current structure's own rules (a partnership change, for instance, requires unanimity of partners). Structure history is preserved on the public record.
organizations_transfersconversions.monop: Monopoly acquisition — the one path that overrides owner consent
organizations_transfersconversions.no_in: No internal restructurings recorded here — structure history renders on each organization's ownership panel.
organizations_transfersconversions.open_: Open this page with to file a transfer, conversion request, or dissolution against a specific organization.
organizations_transfersconversions.owner: Ownership transfers only by mutual consent (, WF-ORG-06): the current owner initiates and the transferee consents. Both consents must be on record; the engine rejects completion with anything less.
organizations_transfersconversions.share: shareholders paid ≥ fair market — the engine blocks underpayment
organizations_transfersconversions.showi: Showing the transfer/conversion register for {name}. Drop the query to see the whole registry.
organizations_transfersconversions.when_: When the legislature finds monopolistic control, it may acquire the enterprise for the public (, WF-ORG-07). This is a legislative act at ordinary majority of all serving — the only path that proceeds without owner consent — and the owners are paid at or above fair market value. It is initiated through the bill flow.
